target.name: Do gene-corrected epidermal stem-cell grafts remain stable and free of clonal or malignant events beyond five years?

summary: A 6.5-year follow-up with integration-site analysis of the first transgenic epidermal stem-cell graft recipient already exists (De Rosa et al., Stem Cell Reports 2014)
rationale: De Rosa L, Carulli S, Cocchiarella F, Quaglino D, Enzo E, ... De Luca M, 'Long-term stability and safety of transgenic cultured epidermal stem cells in gene therapy of junctional epidermolysis bullosa', Stem Cell Reports 2014, doi:10.1016/j.stemcr.2013.11.001. It reports 6.5 years of follow-up of the 2006 Mavilio patient with genome-wide retroviral integration-site analysis, stable transgene expression and no clonal dominance or tumour. The question as written asks for follow-up 'beyond five years' with integration-site analysis; this source meets that for n=1 (retroviral vector, pre-Hirsch 2017). Suggested edits: add the source and a claim at L4 (one group, n=1), attach it to hrm:capability/epidermis-gene-corrected-stem-cell-replacement, and narrow the question to the 2017 whole-body recipient and any Hologene 5 (Phase II/III) recipients. Surfaced by ChatGPT (GPT-5.6, web search) during the 2026-09-14 prediction run, verified in Europe PMC by Claude Code; abstract-level only.
